purpose: Order the 22 countable candidate applications for feasibility work without converting candidate names into empirical denominators.
ordering_policy: prefer an existing local compose, seed, or benchmark asset
prefer a deterministic self-hosted deployment with a narrow independent oracle surface
defer applications with external identity, mail, calendar, storage, or multi-service dependencies
record rejection and infrastructure boundaries before selecting the next application

waves.purpose: Finish or isolate the two candidates with repository-local deployment assets before adding another adapter.
Prefer applications likely to expose stable database/file state and a bounded browser workflow.
Expand interaction diversity after one wave-1 application passes reset and oracle triage.
Defer high-cost or multi-service systems until the harness has stable diagnostics and a repeatable reset budget.

admission_rule: The queue is not evidence and does not authorize execution.
A candidate advances only after source/license, version/digest, deterministic reset, independent oracle, and clean three-arm pilot checks.
A failed deployment is classified as infrastructure evidence and remains outside the success denominator.
Cross-application tasks remain blocked until both endpoint applications are individually admitted.
